name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q01 - Matching minerals with their chemical formulas

questiontext.text:
Match the minerals in List I with their corresponding chemical formulas in List II.

List I (Mineral)List II (Chemical Formula)
(a) Chile saltpetre(i) \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\)
(b) Fluorapatite(ii) \(\mathrm{PbS}\)
(c) Gypsum(iii) \(\mathrm{NaNO_3}\)
(d) Galena(iv) \(\mathrm{Ca_9(PO_4)_6 \cdot CaF_2}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the earth's crust, \(p\)-block elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulphur occur naturally in characteristic nitrate, phosphate, sulphate, and sulphide minerals.

Step 2: Matching Each Mineral
Chile saltpetre is the common name for naturally occurring sodium nitrate, \(\mathrm{NaNO_3}\), which corresponds to (a)-(iii). Fluorapatite is a phosphate rock mineral of the apatite family with formula \(\mathrm{Ca_9(PO_4)_6 \cdot CaF_2}\), giving (b)-(iv). Gypsum is a hydrated calcium sulphate mineral with formula \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\), giving (c)-(i). Galena is the principal sulphide ore of lead with formula \(\mathrm{PbS}\), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q02 - Matching noble gases with their characteristic uses and sources

questiontext.text:
Match the noble gases in List I with their characteristic uses or origin in List II.

List I (Noble Gas)List II (Use / Origin)
(a) Helium(i) Inert atmosphere in arc welding of metals
(b) Neon(ii) Decay product of \({}^{226}\mathrm{Ra}\)
(c) Argon(iii) Diluent for oxygen in modern diving apparatus
(d) Radon(iv) Discharge tubes and fluorescent bulbs for advertisement display

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The practical applications and natural occurrence of Group 18 noble gases depend on their chemical inertness, low boiling points, low blood solubility, and nuclear stability.

Step 2: Matching Each Noble Gas
Helium has very low solubility in blood, so it is used as a diluent for oxygen in modern diving apparatus to prevent decompression sickness, giving (a)-(iii). Neon emits characteristic bright colours in electrical discharges and is used in discharge tubes and fluorescent bulbs for advertisement display, giving (b)-(iv). Argon is abundant in air and provides an inert atmosphere in high-temperature metallurgical processes such as arc welding, giving (c)-(i). Radon is a radioactive noble gas obtained as a decay product of \({}^{226}_{88}\mathrm{Ra}\), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q03 - Matching halogens with their colours and physical states

questiontext.text:
Match the halogens in List I with their colour and physical state at \(298\ \mathrm{K}\) in List II.

List I (Halogen)List II (Colour and Physical State)
(a) \(\mathrm{F_2}\)(i) Red liquid
(b) \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\)(ii) Violet solid
(c) \(\mathrm{Br_2}\)(iii) Yellow gas
(d) \(\mathrm{I_2}\)(iv) Greenish yellow gas

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Halogens absorb radiations in the visible region, exciting outer electrons to higher energy levels, which gives them characteristic colours. Intermolecular van der Waals forces increase down Group 17 as molecular mass increases, causing physical state to change from gas to liquid to solid.

Step 2: Matching Each Halogen
Fluorine (\(\mathrm{F_2}\)) is a yellow gas, giving (a)-(iii). Chlorine (\(\mathrm{Cl_2}\)) is a greenish yellow gas, giving (b)-(iv). Bromine (\(\mathrm{Br_2}\)) is a red liquid, giving (c)-(i). Iodine (\(\mathrm{I_2}\)) is a violet solid, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q04 - Matching oxides of nitrogen with oxidation state and nature

questiontext.text:
Match the oxides of nitrogen in List I with their nitrogen oxidation state and physical appearance/chemical nature in List II.

List I (Oxide)List II (Oxidation State & Nature)
(a) \(\mathrm{N_2O}\)(i) \(+3\), blue solid, acidic
(b) \(\mathrm{NO_2}\)(ii) \(+5\), colourless solid, acidic
(c) \(\mathrm{N_2O_3}\)(iii) \(+1\), colourless gas, neutral
(d) \(\mathrm{N_2O_5}\)(iv) \(+4\), brown gas, acidic

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nitrogen forms oxides in oxidation states from \(+1\) to \(+5\). Lower oxides (\(+1\) and \(+2\)) are neutral, whereas higher oxides (\(+3\), \(+4\), and \(+5\)) are acidic.

Step 2: Oxidation State Calculation and Matching
In \(\mathrm{N_2O}\), \(2x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +1\); it is a colourless, neutral gas, giving (a)-(iii). In \(\mathrm{NO_2}\), \(x + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +4\); it is a brown acidic gas, giving (b)-(iv). In \(\mathrm{N_2O_3}\), \(2x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3\); it is a blue acidic solid, giving (c)-(i). In \(\mathrm{N_2O_5}\), \(2x + 5(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5\); it is a colourless acidic solid, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q05 - Matching oxoacids of phosphorus with characteristic bonds

questiontext.text:
Match the oxoacids of phosphorus in List I with the characteristic bonds present in one molecule in List II.

List I (Oxoacid)List II (Characteristic Bonds)
(a) \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)(i) Two \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), one \(\mathrm{P-H}\), one \(\mathrm{P=O}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)(ii) Four \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), two \(\mathrm{P=O}\), one \(\mathrm{P-O-P}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{H_3PO_4}\)(iii) One \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), two \(\mathrm{P-H}\), one \(\mathrm{P=O}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{H_4P_2O_7}\)(iv) Three \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), one \(\mathrm{P=O}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In all oxoacids of phosphorus, each phosphorus atom is tetrahedrally surrounded and has at least one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) and one \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) bond. Lower oxoacids contain direct \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds, whereas condensed acids contain \(\mathrm{P-O-P}\) linkages.

Step 2: Matching Each Oxoacid
Hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) has one \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), two \(\mathrm{P-H}\), and one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) bond, giving (a)-(iii). Orthophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)) has two \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), one \(\mathrm{P-H}\), and one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) bond, giving (b)-(i). Orthophosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_4}\)) has three \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) and one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) bond, giving (c)-(iv). Pyrophosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H_4P_2O_7}\)) has four \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), two \(\mathrm{P=O}\), and one \(\mathrm{P-O-P}\) bond, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q06 - Matching simple oxides with their chemical classification

questiontext.text:
Match the oxides in List I with their chemical classification in List II.

List I (Oxide)List II (Classification)
(a) \(\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}\)(i) Neutral oxide
(b) \(\mathrm{CaO}\)(ii) Amphoteric oxide
(c) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)(iii) Basic oxide
(d) \(\mathrm{N_2O}\)(iv) Acidic oxide

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Simple oxides are classified as acidic (combine with water to form acids), basic (combine with water to form bases), amphoteric (react with both acids and alkalies), or neutral (neither acidic nor basic).

Step 2: Matching Each Oxide
\(\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}\) is a non-metal oxide in a high oxidation state (\(+7\)) that reacts with water to form perchloric acid, so it is an acidic oxide, giving (a)-(iv). \(\mathrm{CaO}\) is a metallic oxide that combines with water to give \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\), making it a basic oxide, giving (b)-(iii). \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) reacts with both \(\mathrm{HCl}\) and \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), so it is an amphoteric oxide, giving (c)-(ii). \(\mathrm{N_2O}\) (along with \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{NO}\)) is neither acidic nor basic, so it is a neutral oxide, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q07 - Matching industrial processes with the chemicals manufactured

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial processes in List I with the chemicals manufactured by them in List II.

List I (Process)List II (Chemical Manufactured)
(a) Haber's process(i) Chlorine (\(\mathrm{Cl_2}\))
(b) Ostwald's process(ii) Sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\))
(c) Contact process(iii) Ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_3}\))
(d) Deacon's process(iv) Nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\))

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Major inorganic \(p\)-block chemicals are manufactured on a large scale using dedicated catalytic processes.

Step 2: Matching Each Process
Haber's process synthesises ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_3}\)) from \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2}\), giving (a)-(iii). Ostwald's process manufactures nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) by catalytic oxidation of \(\mathrm{NH_3}\), giving (b)-(iv). Contact process manufactures sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)) via catalytic oxidation of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_3}\), giving (c)-(ii). Deacon's process produces chlorine (\(\mathrm{Cl_2}\)) by oxidising \(\mathrm{HCl}\) gas with atmospheric oxygen, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q08 - Matching industrial reactions with their catalysts

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions in List I with the catalysts used in List II.

List I (Reaction)List II (Catalyst)
(a) \(\mathrm{N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3}\)(i) \(\mathrm{CuCl_2}\)
(b) \(4\mathrm{NH_3 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 4NO + 6H_2O}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\)
(c) \(2\mathrm{SO_2 + O_2 \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3}\)(iii) Iron oxide with \(\mathrm{K_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
(d) \(4\mathrm{HCl + O_2 \rightarrow 2Cl_2 + 2H_2O}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{Pt/Rh}\) gauze

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each industrial synthesis in \(p\)-block chemistry uses a specific heterogeneous catalyst to achieve practical reaction rates at optimum temperature and pressure.

Step 2: Matching Each Reaction
Ammonia synthesis in Haber's process uses iron oxide with small amounts of \(\mathrm{K_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\), giving (a)-(iii). Oxidation of ammonia to nitric oxide in Ostwald's process uses a \(\mathrm{Pt/Rh}\) gauze catalyst at \(500\ \mathrm{K}\) and \(9\ \mathrm{bar}\), giving (b)-(iv). Oxidation of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_3}\) in the Contact process uses \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) at \(720\ \mathrm{K}\), giving (c)-(ii). Oxidation of \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) in Deacon's process uses \(\mathrm{CuCl_2}\) at \(723\ \mathrm{K}\), giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q09 - Matching oxoacids of sulphur with their structural features

questiontext.text:
Match the oxoacids of sulphur in List I with their characteristic structural features in List II.

List I (Oxoacid of Sulphur)List II (Structural Feature)
(a) Sulphurous acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\))(i) Contains an \(\mathrm{S-O-O-S}\) peroxide linkage
(b) Sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\))(ii) Contains an \(\mathrm{S-O-S}\) oxo-bridge linkage
(c) Pyrosulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\))(iii) Central \(\mathrm{S}\) has one lone pair, one \(\mathrm{S=O}\), and two \(\mathrm{S-OH}\) bonds
(d) Peroxodisulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}\))(iv) Central \(\mathrm{S}\) has zero lone pairs, two \(\mathrm{S=O}\), and two \(\mathrm{S-OH}\) bonds

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sulphur exhibits \(+4\) or \(+6\) oxidation state in its common oxoacids, which determines the number of \(\mathrm{S=O}\) bonds, \(\mathrm{S-OH}\) bonds, lone pairs, and bridging oxygen atoms.

Step 2: Matching Each Oxoacid
In sulphurous acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\)), sulphur is in the \(+4\) oxidation state and retains one lone pair along with one \(\mathrm{S=O}\) and two \(\mathrm{S-OH}\) bonds, giving (a)-(iii). In sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)), sulphur is in the \(+6\) oxidation state with zero lone pairs, two \(\mathrm{S=O}\) bonds, and two \(\mathrm{S-OH}\) bonds, giving (b)-(iv). Pyrosulphuric acid (oleum, \(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\)) consists of two \(\mathrm{SO_3H}\) units joined by an \(\mathrm{S-O-S}\) bridge, giving (c)-(ii). Peroxodisulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}\)) has two sulphur centres joined by an \(\mathrm{S-O-O-S}\) peroxide linkage, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q10 - Matching redox reactions of nitric acid and chlorine with their products

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions in List I with the characteristic products formed in List II.

List I (Reaction)List II (Characteristic Products)
(a) \(\mathrm{Cu + HNO_3\ (dilute)}\)(i) \(\mathrm{N_2O}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{Cu + HNO_3\ (conc.)}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{NaCl + NaClO_3}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{Zn + HNO_3\ (dilute)}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{NO}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{Cl_2 + NaOH\ (hot\ and\ conc.)}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{NO_2}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The reduction product of nitric acid depends on acid concentration and the reducing strength of the metal, while chlorine undergoes disproportionation in hot concentrated alkali.

Step 2: Matching Each Reaction
Copper reacts with dilute \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) to liberate \(\mathrm{NO}\) gas (\(3\mathrm{Cu} + 8\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2} + 2\mathrm{NO} + 4\mathrm{H_2O}\)), giving (a)-(iii). Copper reacts with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) to liberate brown \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) gas (\(\mathrm{Cu} + 4\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2} + 2\mathrm{NO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\)), giving (b)-(iv). Zinc reacts with dilute \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) to form \(\mathrm{N_2O}\) (\(4\mathrm{Zn} + 10\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{Zn(NO_3)_2} + 5\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{N_2O}\)), giving (c)-(i). Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to give sodium chloride and sodium chlorate (\(6\mathrm{NaOH} + 3\mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow 5\mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{NaClO_3} + 3\mathrm{H_2O}\)), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q11 - Matching oxides and oxyfluorides with their specific applications

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds in List I with their specific applications in List II.

List I (Compound)List II (Application)
(a) \(\mathrm{ClO_2}\)(i) Removing plutonium as \(\mathrm{PuF_6}\) from spent nuclear fuel
(b) \(\mathrm{I_2O_5}\)(ii) Anti-chlor and refining of petroleum and sugar
(c) \(\mathrm{O_2F_2}\)(iii) Bleaching agent for paper pulp and textiles
(d) \(\mathrm{SO_2}\)(iv) Quantitative estimation of carbon monoxide

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Halogen oxides, oxygen fluorides, and sulphur dioxide possess strong oxidising, fluorinating, or reducing/bleaching properties that make them useful in specific industrial and analytical applications.

Step 2: Matching Each Compound
Chlorine dioxide (\(\mathrm{ClO_2}\)) is used as a bleaching agent for paper pulp and textiles and in water treatment, giving (a)-(iii). Iodine pentoxide (\(\mathrm{I_2O_5}\)) is a very good oxidising agent used in the estimation of carbon monoxide, giving (b)-(iv). Dioxygen difluoride (\(\mathrm{O_2F_2}\)) oxidises plutonium to \(\mathrm{PuF_6}\) and is used in removing plutonium from spent nuclear fuel, giving (c)-(i). Sulphur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO_2}\)) is used in refining petroleum and sugar and as an anti-chlor, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q12 - Matching interhalogen compounds with their molecular structures

questiontext.text:
Match the interhalogen compounds in List I with their molecular structures or solid-state forms in List II.

List I (Interhalogen)List II (Structure / Form)
(a) \(\mathrm{ClF_3}\)(i) Pentagonal bipyramidal
(b) \(\mathrm{BrF_5}\)(ii) Dimerises as \(\mathrm{Cl}\)-bridged \(\mathrm{I_2Cl_6}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{IF_7}\)(iii) Bent T-shaped
(d) \(\mathrm{ICl_3}\)(iv) Square pyramidal

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The shapes of interhalogen compounds \(\mathrm{XX'_n}\) are determined by VSEPR theory from the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around the larger central halogen atom \(\mathrm{X}\).

Step 2: Matching Each Interhalogen
In \(\mathrm{ClF_3}\) (\(\mathrm{XX'_3}\)), \(\mathrm{Cl}\) has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (\(sp^3d\)), giving a bent T-shaped structure, so (a)-(iii). In \(\mathrm{BrF_5}\) (\(\mathrm{XX'_5}\)), \(\mathrm{Br}\) has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (\(sp^3d^2\)), giving a square pyramidal structure, so (b)-(iv). In \(\mathrm{IF_7}\) (\(\mathrm{XX'_7}\)), \(\mathrm{I}\) has 7 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^3d^3\)), giving a pentagonal bipyramidal structure, so (c)-(i). \(\mathrm{ICl_3}\) dimerises as a chlorine-bridged dimer \(\mathrm{I_2Cl_6}\), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q13 - Matching xenon compounds with their molecular shapes

questiontext.text:
Match the xenon compounds in List I with their molecular shapes in List II.

List I (Xenon Compound)List II (Molecular Shape)
(a) \(\mathrm{XeF_2}\)(i) Distorted octahedral
(b) \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\)(ii) Pyramidal
(c) \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\)(iii) Linear
(d) \(\mathrm{XeO_3}\)(iv) Square planar

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Using VSEPR theory, the molecular geometry is determined by the number of \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and lone pairs around the central \(\mathrm{Xe}\) atom.

Step 2: Matching Each Xenon Compound
In \(\mathrm{XeF_2}\), \(\mathrm{Xe}\) has 2 bond pairs and 3 equatorial lone pairs (\(sp^3d\)), giving a linear shape, so (a)-(iii). In \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\), \(\mathrm{Xe}\) has 4 bond pairs and 2 trans lone pairs (\(sp^3d^2\)), giving a square planar shape, so (b)-(iv). In \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\), \(\mathrm{Xe}\) has 6 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (\(sp^3d^3\)), giving a distorted octahedral shape, so (c)-(i). In \(\mathrm{XeO_3}\), \(\mathrm{Xe}\) forms three \(\mathrm{Xe=O}\) double bonds and retains 1 lone pair (\(sp^3\)), giving a pyramidal shape, so (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q14 - Matching halogen anions with isostructural noble gas species

questiontext.text:
Match the halogen species in List I with their isostructural noble gas species in List II.

List I (Halogen Species)List II (Isostructural Noble Gas Species)
(a) \(\mathrm{ICl_4^-}\)(i) \(\mathrm{XeO_3}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{IBr_2^-}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{BrO_3^-}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{BrF_5}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{XeF_2}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Species are isostructural when they have the same number of \(\sigma\)-bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom, resulting in identical molecular geometry.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
In \(\mathrm{ICl_4^-}\), iodine has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (square planar), which is isostructural with \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\), giving (a)-(iii). In \(\mathrm{IBr_2^-}\), iodine has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs (linear), which is isostructural with \(\mathrm{XeF_2}\), giving (b)-(iv). In \(\mathrm{BrO_3^-}\), bromine has 3 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 1 lone pair (pyramidal), which is isostructural with \(\mathrm{XeO_3}\), giving (c)-(i). In \(\mathrm{BrF_5}\), bromine has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (square pyramidal), which is isostructural with \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q15 - Matching hydrolysis reactions with their products

questiontext.text:
Match the hydrolysis reactions in List I with the products obtained in List II.

List I (Hydrolysis Reaction)List II (Products)
(a) \(2\mathrm{XeF_2(s) + 2H_2O(l)}\)(i) \(\mathrm{XeO_3 + 6HF}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{XeF_6 + 3H_2O}\) (complete)(ii) \(\mathrm{HX' + HOX}\) (where \(\mathrm{X}\) is larger)
(c) \(\mathrm{XeF_6 + H_2O}\) (partial)(iii) \(2\mathrm{Xe(g) + 4HF(aq) + O_2(g)}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{XX' + H_2O}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{XeOF_4 + 2HF}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Xenon fluorides undergo redox or non-redox hydrolysis depending on the oxidation state of xenon, whereas interhalogens \(\mathrm{XX'}\) hydrolyse to form a hydrohalic acid of the smaller halogen and a hypohalous acid of the larger halogen.

Step 2: Matching Each Hydrolysis Reaction
\(\mathrm{XeF_2}\) hydrolyses to give \(\mathrm{Xe}\), \(\mathrm{HF}\), and \(\mathrm{O_2}\) (\(2\mathrm{XeF_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Xe} + 4\mathrm{HF} + \mathrm{O_2}\)), giving (a)-(iii). Complete hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\) with 3 moles of water gives explosive \(\mathrm{XeO_3}\) and \(6\mathrm{HF}\), giving (b)-(i). Partial hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\) with 1 mole of water gives \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\) and \(2\mathrm{HF}\), giving (c)-(iv). Hydrolysis of an interhalogen \(\mathrm{XX'}\) yields \(\mathrm{HX'}\) (from the smaller, more electronegative halogen) and \(\mathrm{HOX}\) (from the larger halogen), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q16 - Matching p-block extreme physical and thermodynamic properties with elements

questiontext.text:
Match the extreme properties in List I with the corresponding \(p\)-block elements or molecules in List II.

List I (Property)List II (Element / Molecule)
(a) Most negative electron gain enthalpy among halogens(i) \(\mathrm{He}\)
(b) Highest \(\mathrm{X-X}\) bond dissociation enthalpy among halogens(ii) \(\mathrm{F_2}\)
(c) Strongest oxidising agent among halogens in aqueous solution(iii) \(\mathrm{Cl}\)
(d) Lowest boiling point (\(4.2\ \mathrm{K}\)) of any known substance(iv) \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Anomalies in second-period elements (such as fluorine) and weak dispersion forces in monoatomic noble gases produce characteristic extreme values in electron gain enthalpy, bond dissociation enthalpy, electrode potential, and boiling point.

Step 2: Matching Each Property
